chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said on his pulpit:
Indeed, the best of names are Abdullah, Abd al-Rahman, Haritha, and Himam. And the worst of names are Dirar, Murrat, Harb, and Zalim.

key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ: Abd al-Rahman (Servant of the Most Merciful)

ai.seo_question: What are the best and worst names in Islam according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the semantic weight of names in Shia tradition, linking 'Abdullah' and 'Abd al-Rahman' to core theological concepts of servitude and divine attributes. The inclusion of 'Haritha' (agriculturist/provider) and 'Himam' (ambitious) alongside 'Dirar' (harm) and 'Harb' (war) illustrates the belief that a name influences the bearer's character and destiny, a view supported by scholars like al-Saduq as a reflection of spiritual reality.
